page.layout: One page of text. Top centre: page number "(8)". Below it: the heading "SECT. 5." with the title "De Vocalibus, & Diphthongis." Then one running paragraph. Then a two-column table of vowel signs (Hebrew sign and value), with a sub-heading above each half ("Vocales longæ", "Breves"). Below the table: the Scheva paragraph and a numbered list. At the bottom right: the catchword "Ante-". No running head, no margin notes.

main_text.head: SECT. 5.
De Vocalibus, & Diphthongis.
main_text.p: Vocales sunt 5 longæ, totidemque breves, quibus addunt quidam Scheva simplex & compositum.
main_text.head: Vocales longæ.
main_text.l: Camets | אָ | valet a longum, obscurū.
Tsere | אֵ | e longum, ut η Græc.
Chirec longum, feu magnum | אִ | i longum.
Schurec | אֻ | u longum, vel υ Græcorum.
main_text.head: Breves:
main_text.l: Chirec breve, feu parvum | אִ | i breve.

page.notes: The Hebrew vowel points are approximated as alef carrier plus the point (Unicode Hebrew points); the printed glyphs are small and the carrier and point shapes are not certain, especially for Cholem, Schurec and the Scheva. The Greek letters η and υ are read from small print and may be doubtful. The printed "Breves:" may have a colon or semicolon. Printed "ut" in the Tsere line appears bold, not italic.
